Introduction

West Virginia licenses Personal Care Agencies (In-Home) to provide non-medical personal care services. The WV Department of Health — Office of Health Facility Licensure & Certification oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand West Virginia’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand West Virginia’s Regulations

WV DOH licenses personal care agencies under state regulations. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the WV Secretary of State, apply for personal care agency license, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

WV benchmarks: Private pay rates $18-$26/hour, Medicaid rates $14-$20/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

WV requires background checks and training for all personal care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting WV DOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Charleston, Huntington, Morgantown, and statewide.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
